director.chapterArc: High-stakes physical exertion transitioning to tactical crisis, then mechanical resolution, ending on quiet exhaustion.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Callie's internal arithmetic rhythm during the pull; do not let the action become a generic shout-fest. The horror is in the silence of her mother and the coldness of the steel, not screaming.

cues.delivery: Internal focus on physical sensation; the cold is a tangible weight. Subtext: The realization of failure before it happens.
cues.from: The cold was in her hand. It was in her wrist.
cues.through: She could not help it. The whole wagon was on it, and Pell, and the load that was going to buy a table at Meridian. She knelt there with her palm flat on the back of the forged curve, and watched the pale in the steel the way she had watched her mother breathe every night since Gaunt's Reach. And as she watched, her fingers closed round the curve. She did not tell them to. They closed, the way they had always closed on anything that mattered, and held on.
cues.reason: Shift from external observation to internal panic and self-awareness.

cues.delivery: Sharp, urgent command. Subtext: Desperate attempt to stop the momentum.
cues.through: Pell hauled the brake. It shrieked on the tyre, and the wagon went back. It went back a foot, a foot and a half, grinding on the rock with the chocks skidding under the rear wheels. Then the off chock found a step in the rock and jammed, and the near one jammed behind it, and the wagon stopped.
cues.reason: Genuine shouted command in a crisis moment.

cues.delivery: Mother's voice is distant but piercingly clear. Subtext: The only solution to the panic.
cues.through: "You said yesterday it held when you weren't looking at it," her mother said. "When you turned round and talked to Otto about the strap. I heard you tell Katori. So don't look at it. Look at me."
cues.reason: Shift from Callie's internal struggle to external guidance.

cues.delivery: Deliberate, almost ritualistic. Subtext: Trusting the mechanism over instinct.
cues.from: She did it before she could think about it. She did it the way you take your hand off a baby's back once you're sure it's asleep, slowly, not quite believing. And she stood up in the road beside the hook with her hands empty at her sides. She kept her feet planted, and she turned her head, and looked up at her mother on the rim.
cues.through: She felt it come on, far away, like wind on a house. She felt the hook take it. She felt it the way she felt her own tongue, the way she'd felt the Edge on the causeway, a pace away from her and hers. It was not in her hands. It was not in her body at all. It was in the steel. The steel was standing in the rock the way her back foot stood in the road, and all she had to do was not argue with it.
cues.reason: The breakthrough moment of letting go.

cues.delivery: Tactical realization. Subtext: The shift in threat dynamics.
cues.from: Callie heard Katori's Ember come out.
cues.through: "Thirty-four," said Ines. Then, in the same breath, in a completely different voice: "Forty paces. Taking it."
cues.reason: Katori's action changes the scene from a pull to an ambush.

cues.delivery: Otto shouting 'UP' is frantic but controlled. Subtext: The horse's panic and the need for direction.
cues.from: There was a noise from the top that was Duchess, a high, terrible, ringing noise. And there was Otto's voice under it. He was not talking any more. He was shouting, one word, the same one, over and over.
cues.through: The wagon came up the pitch at a speed that no wagon had any business going up a pitch at. Callie heard it come. The wheels were grinding on the rock and the chocks were bouncing on their ropes, and Pell was saying "Easy, easy, easy," to nobody, with his hands off the brake. At the top, the mare was leaving. She was leaving as hard as a horse can leave, straight up the road away from the things coming down it, because Otto had got her head round and pointed it away from them, and let her go.
cues.reason: Genuine shouted command in a crisis moment.

cues.delivery: Mechanical precision. Subtext: The physics of the kill.
cues.from: It was one. Katori had one of the others. Callie could hear her fifty paces out on the high plain, working. Ines had put the second down on the road with two arrows. This was the third. It had come past all of it, straight past the lit woman with the blade, straight past the horse and the boy. It came over the lip and down the fifteen paces of road toward her on all four points, its head low and its long arms out, going for the brightest thing on the hill.
cues.through: She did not remember going. She remembered the rock of the cut wall, suddenly, at the side of her head and all down her left side. She remembered sitting in the road. She remembered the taste of blood, and not being able to breathe in. She could only breathe halfway in before something in her side said no.
cues.reason: The husk's movement and Callie's reaction are described as physical facts.

cues.delivery: Instinctual action. Subtext: The body knowing what the mind cannot process.
cues.from: She did not think about it. There was no time for thinking. There was only the thing her body had known since before she could remember knowing it. You don't stab a husk. You step across. You don't step back.
cues.through: The husk came apart. It came apart all at once and from everywhere, while it was still turning, the way a sack loses its bottom. What had been a husk was a grey haze hanging in the air of the cut, and then settling, and then running in a long thin tongue down the slope of the road, past her boots, into the pitch.
cues.reason: The physical resolution of the combat.

cues.delivery: Pell's roar is a command to stop. Subtext: Relief mixed with adrenaline.
cues.reason: Genuine shouted command in a crisis moment.

cues.delivery: Quiet exhaustion. Subtext: The acceptance of emptiness.
cues.from: She went down into herself to look.
cues.through: She lay in the road at the top of the scarp and looked up at the sky, and breathed halfway in, and halfway out, and counted.
cues.reason: Shift from action to internal reflection.

pauses.after: The cold was in her hand. It was in her wrist.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on physical sensation before the realization of failure.

pauses.after: Callie knelt in the road with her head down and her arm dead to the shoulder. She could not feel her fingers at all.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: The wagon has stopped short; Callie is injured and exhausted.
Speaker reset for Mother's voice cutting through the silence.

pauses.after: It was the hardest thing she had ever done. It was harder than the causeway or the span, or walking out of the pump house doorway. Every part of her wanted to look down and see if it was still pale. She didn't. She looked at her mother's hat, and the red earth, and the edge of Ines's bow against the sky.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: The realization of what she must do (look away).
Contrast to previous dialogue; marks the shift in tone.

pauses.after: "The top," said her mother. "The road. Past the horse. Three of them."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset for the shift in threat direction.
Major emotional landing: The horse's panic and the line going tight.
Setup for the reversal that it is not her.
Speaker reset for the revelation that the hook is the target.

pauses.before: She remembered sitting in the road.
pauses.reason: Emphasis on the physical sensation of impact and disorientation.

pauses.after: "Callie!" That was her mother. "It's on three! Callie, it's on three — "
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the injury before the action resumes.
Climax of the combat sequence; marks the resolution.

pauses.after: The pitch eased. It eased a few paces below the seam, where the rock went over into the gentler slope that ran up to the lip. The front wheels came over onto it. The rear wheels came over onto it. And the grinding stopped, because the wagon was not going up a wall any more. It was going up a road.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset for Pell's command as the wagon clears the pitch.

pauses.before: It was dry right down to the stone
pauses.reason: Emphasis on the depth of her exhaustion and emptiness.

pauses.after: She lay in the road at the top of the scarp and looked up at the sky, and breathed halfway in, and halfway out, and counted.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: The final count and acceptance of emptiness.
